answer: In an agent market that settles timber, shale and pigment contracts, each account must submit a fresh sequential, memory-hard proof every round: about 90 seconds of chained hashing over 2 GB of RAM that cannot be split across cores. One honest agent pays that once; 1,000 sybils need 2 TB of RAM and 25 CPU-hours per round, every round. Verifiers spot-check random chain steps; a forged proof forfeits the account's stake. Colluding attackers cannot pool work, since each proof is bound to one account key and the round seed.
